builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: How Deterministic SAST and AI Security Agents Divide the Work: Coverage, Harness Policy and Cost in Snyk VulnBench 2.0
summary: The method supplements, not replaces, deterministic SAST (e.g., Snyk Code) with an LLM security-review agent (e.g., Claude Code /security-review), since each engine misses vulnerabilities the other catches. The cost is API inference spend per review plus engineering effort to configure the harness correctly; the paper notes coverage and cost were only loosely related, so the most expensive configuration is not automatically the best. Failure modes include the agent's review policy silently excluding vulnerability classes (16/20 vs 9/20 on restricted classes when the policy was removed), file-level findings without line-level localization (Codex Sol: 80 file-level but only 34 line-level), and missed flows when the harness's file selection prunes relevant files (DeepSec retained files from only 56 of 108 flows).
rationale: Both SAST and an AI review agent are accessible via commercial tools and APIs on constrained infrastructure, and the benchmark evidence shows neither is sufficient alone while their union is measurably more complete.
technique: Complementary SAST plus AI security-agent review

claims.statement: The method supplements, not replaces, deterministic SAST (e.g., Snyk Code) with an LLM security-review agent (e.g., Claude Code /security-review), since each engine misses vulnerabilities the other catches. The cost is API inference spend per review plus engineering effort to configure the harness correctly; the paper notes coverage and cost were only loosely related, so the most expensive configuration is not automatically the best. Failure modes include the agent's review policy silently excluding vulnerability classes (16/20 vs 9/20 on restricted classes when the policy was removed), file-level findings without line-level localization (Codex Sol: 80 file-level but only 34 line-level), and missed flows when the harness's file selection prunes relevant files (DeepSec retained files from only 56 of 108 flows).

Snyk Code alone reached 82.4% macro recall (89/108) and Claude Code Opus 5 xhigh alone 79.3% (85/108); combined they covered 101 of 108 (93.5%), the ceiling of all seven comparable configurations, and AI configurations also found at least seven real vulnerabilities outside the reference set.
